# Search Engine Optimization Services

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/seo

> YB Marketing provides expert SEO services for businesses in Yakima and across the country, helping businesses rank higher and get found online. Call 509-901-9735 for a free site review.

## Rank Higher. Drive More Traffic.

Most people who search online don't have the time or the desire to wade through pages of results. As a business owner, you probably aren't interested in learning the complicated (and ever-changing) matrix behind SEO, but we are. We do SEO and we can help your business.

### What Is Search Engine Optimization?

Most people who search online don't wade through pages of results — they click the top few. SEO is the science of getting your business there. We handle the ever-changing algorithm so you don't have to.

### What It Looks Like When It Works

Three local service businesses that came to us with almost no search visibility. Here's where they ended up.
We built service, equipment and location pages across dozens of regional markets so they show up wherever their customers search.
We fixed the technical problems holding the site back, then built out service and location pages for searches like "brake repair" and "tire shop near me."
We added pages for panel upgrades, EV chargers and emergency repair, and strengthened their Google Business Profile to compete in the map pack.

### Start With the Problem You Actually Have

#### Local SEO

For businesses that serve a city or region. We work on the map pack, your service and location pages, and the directory listings Google uses to double check you're real.

#### Google Business Profile

Your profile is often the first thing people see, before they ever reach your website. We set it up properly, keep it active with photos and posts, and help you collect more reviews.

#### AI Search (GEO)

ChatGPT and Google's AI Overviews recommend businesses based on sources they trust. We work on getting you into those sources, and we track where you're being mentioned.

#### Technical SEO

Slow pages, broken links, pages Google can't index. Nobody's favorite part of SEO, and very often the reason good content doesn't rank.

#### SEO Audits

A full look at where you stand and a ranked list of what to fix. Useful before a redesign, or when you're not sure what your current agency is doing.

#### Website Migrations

A new website or a new domain is the fastest way to lose rankings you spent years earning. We map every old page to its new home so you keep them.

### What Happens After You Sign

SEO has a reputation for being a black box. Here's exactly what we do, in order, and what you'll see along the way.
- 1 Month 1 Audit, Tracking and Fixes Audit. We look at your rankings, your website's technical health, your Google Business Profile and your top competitors. You get our findings in plain English. Tracking. Before we change anything, we make sure conversions and rankings are being measured. Otherwise there's no way to prove what worked. Fixes. The technical problems, profile cleanup and directory listings come first. They're the quickest wins and everything else depends on them.
- 2 Month 2 onward Content We build or rewrite the pages that match what your customers search for: service pages, location pages, and clear answers to the questions they ask before they call.
- 3 Every month Reporting A report showing rankings, traffic, and conversions with recommendations and observations each month.

### Which Is Right for Your Business?

Pay-per-click (PPC) advertising offers immediate visibility and control, while SEO builds organic, sustainable traffic over time. Many businesses benefit from both. Get in touch with YB to find the right mix for your goals.
- ✓ Long-term, sustainable organic traffic
- ✓ Builds authority and trust with Google
- ✓ Compounds in value — results grow over time
- ✓ Ranks in both traditional and AI search results
- ✓ Immediate visibility at the top of Google
- ✓ Full control over budget and targeting
- ✓ Great for promotions, launches, and events
- ✓ Measurable ROI on every dollar spent

### Frequently Asked Questions

**What is SEO?**
SEO, or search engine optimization, helps your website appear higher in Google and other search results when people search for your products or services.

**How long does SEO take to work?**
SEO is a long-term strategy. Some improvements can happen within a few months, but stronger results usually build over time as content, authority, and rankings improve.

**What SEO services do you provide?**
We help with keyword research, website optimization, content creation, local SEO, technical SEO, reporting, and ongoing strategy.

**Can SEO help my business show up in AI search results?**
Yes. Strong SEO content, clear page structure, FAQs, local relevance, and helpful answers can improve how your business appears in Google AI Overviews and other AI-driven search experiences.

**Do you offer local SEO?**
Yes. We help businesses improve visibility in specific cities and service areas through location pages, Google Business Profile optimization, localized content, and review strategy.

**Do I need new content for SEO?**
In most cases, yes. Search engines need helpful, relevant content to understand what your business offers and where you provide services.

**How do you measure SEO success?**
We look at rankings, impressions, clicks, website traffic, leads, form submissions, phone calls, and growth in important service or location-based searches.

**Is SEO better than Google Ads?**
SEO and Google Ads work differently. SEO builds long-term organic visibility, while Google Ads can generate faster paid traffic. Many businesses benefit from using both together.

# Local SEO Services for Contractors & Service Businesses

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/seo/local-seo

> Help customers in your service area find your business on Google Maps and in local search. Local SEO services with clear reporting on rankings and leads.

## Get found by customers in your service area

When someone searches for an electrician, plumber, or roofing company nearby, you want your business to be one of the options they see. We help service businesses improve their visibility on Google Maps and in local search results.

### What is local SEO?

Local SEO helps your business appear when people search for services in a particular city or area. That includes Google Maps, your Google Business Profile, and the regular search results for the services you offer.
A big part of the work is making sure Google has accurate information about your business. But that isn't enough on its own. Your website also needs useful pages about your services, clear information about where you work, and a consistent presence across other websites and directories.
Your location will always influence where you appear on Google Maps. We focus on the other factors you can improve, from your business profile to the content on your website.
- Google Maps
- Your Google Business Profile
- Regular search results
- Directories like Yelp, Bing, and Apple Maps

### Helping an electrical contractor reach more customers through search

A residential and commercial electrical contractor serving the Greater Bay Area had an established business and a solid reputation. Most of its new work, however, came through paid advertising and subcontractor referrals. The website wasn't bringing in much traffic from people searching for electrical services.
We expanded the site's service and location content, improved the company's Google Business Profile and directory listings, and monitored rankings and leads as the campaign progressed.

### Our local SEO services

#### Google Business Profile optimization

We review your categories, services, business details, photos, and other profile information to make sure customers can find accurate, useful information about your company.

#### Service page development

Customers search for specific services, not just broad business categories. We create and improve pages around the work you want to attract, whether that's electrical panel upgrades, EV charger installation, or another service.

#### Location pages

If you serve several cities or communities, your website should make that clear. We develop location pages that reflect the services you provide in each area, rather than repeating the same copy with a different city name.

#### Business listings

We review your information across relevant directories, including Yelp, Bing, Apple Maps, and industry specific websites. Inconsistent contact details can confuse customers and search engines alike.

#### Review strategy

Customer reviews help people decide whom to contact. We can help you establish a straightforward process for requesting genuine reviews and responding to customer feedback.

#### Rankings and lead reporting

We monitor local search visibility and report on the calls, form submissions, and other leads your website generates, using the tracking available for your business.

### How we work

- 1 Review your current visibility We look at where your business appears in local results, how your Google Business Profile is set up, and how your website compares with local competitors.
- 2 Address the basics We correct business information, improve your profile, and resolve listing issues that may be affecting visibility.
- 3 Improve your website We prioritize the service and location pages most relevant to your business goals.
- 4 Strengthen your local presence We continue working on reviews, relevant listings, and opportunities for local mentions and links.
- 5 Measure results Each month, we review rankings and available lead data to decide where to focus next.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**How is local SEO different from traditional SEO?**
Traditional SEO helps a website appear for relevant searches more broadly. Local SEO focuses on people searching in a specific geographic area, including Google Maps and searches with local intent.

**Do I need a physical address to appear on Google Maps?**
A Google Business Profile generally requires a legitimate business location that meets Google's eligibility rules. If you visit customers rather than serving them at your address, you may be able to hide the address and list your service area instead.

**Why don't I appear in every city I serve?**
Distance is an important factor in Google's local map results. You may have a harder time appearing on the map in areas farther from your business location. Well developed location pages can still help your website appear in the regular search results for those areas.

**How long does local SEO take?**
It depends on your current website, competition, and service area. Some profile and listing improvements may have an effect within weeks, while new service and location pages often take several months to gain traction.

**Can you help us get more reviews?**
Yes. We can help you build a process for asking customers to leave honest reviews and responding to the feedback you receive. We don't purchase or fabricate reviews.

# AI Search Optimization Services (GEO)

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/seo/ai-search

> Improve how your business appears in ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, and other AI search experiences with a strategy built on strong SEO fundamentals.

## Help customers find your business through AI search

Customers are starting to use tools like ChatGPT and Google's AI search features to research services and compare businesses. We help make sure your website and business information are clear, accurate, and easier for these tools to find and reference.

### What is AI search optimization?

AI search optimization, sometimes called generative engine optimization (GEO), focuses on improving how your business is represented in AI generated search answers.
Someone might ask an AI tool which HVAC companies serve their area, what a particular home repair should cost, or how to choose a contractor. Depending on the tool and the question, the answer may include business names, website links, or information gathered from multiple sources.
There isn't a separate trick that guarantees a mention. Much of the work starts with the same things that matter in SEO: accurate business details, useful service pages, a technically accessible website, and a credible presence beyond your own site. We build on that foundation and pay attention to the questions people are asking through AI search.
- ChatGPT
- Google AI Overviews and AI Mode
- Gemini
- Perplexity

### Customers are researching businesses in new ways

A customer who once compared several Google results may now start by asking an AI tool for an explanation or recommendation. Your business needs to be easy to understand wherever that research takes place.
AI answers vary by platform, wording, and available sources. That's why we look at both traditional search performance and how your business appears in relevant AI responses. The goal is to understand where you're visible, where competitors are being mentioned, and what information could be improved.

### Building on measurable SEO improvements

Our work for a Bay Area electrical contractor included improvements to service and location content, local listings, and the overall search presence of the business.

### What we focus on

#### Accurate business information

We review how your services, locations, and company details appear across your website and relevant third party profiles. Consistency helps people and search systems understand what your business does.

#### Content that answers real questions

We improve key pages so they address the questions customers ask before making a purchase or contacting a business. The writing should be useful to people first, while making important information easy for search tools to identify.

#### Technical SEO and structured data

We check whether important pages can be accessed and read by relevant crawlers. We also review structured data where appropriate to help describe your business and services.

#### Reviews and third party visibility

We look at relevant directories, customer reviews, and other websites that mention your business. These sources can help establish a clearer picture of your company beyond what appears on your own site.

#### AI search monitoring

We test relevant questions across supported AI search tools and record whether your business is mentioned, how it is described, and which competitors appear. Because AI answers can change, we treat these results as a snapshot and look for patterns over time.

### How we work

- 1 Establish a starting point We choose questions relevant to your services and locations, then review the responses from the AI platforms included in your tracking.
- 2 Review your online presence We check your website, business profiles, technical setup, and other information sources for gaps or inconsistencies.
- 3 Improve priority pages We update important service content so it answers common customer questions clearly and accurately.
- 4 Work on supporting signals We address relevant listings, review opportunities, and other credible mentions of your business.
- 5 Check progress We repeat the agreed upon tests and review changes alongside your broader SEO performance.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**Is AI search optimization the same as SEO?**
They overlap considerably. A well structured website, useful content, and accurate business information can support both. AI search optimization adds a focus on how your business appears in generated answers and how those appearances are monitored.

**Can you guarantee that ChatGPT will recommend my business?**
No. AI responses change, and no agency controls which businesses an AI tool mentions. We can improve the information available about your business and track its appearance in relevant responses.

**Which AI platforms do you monitor?**
Our coverage includes ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Gemini, and Perplexity.

**Do I need AI search optimization if I'm already investing in SEO?**
You may already have a good starting point. We would first review your existing SEO work and identify whether additional content, technical improvements, or AI visibility monitoring would be worthwhile.

**How can I tell whether my business appears in AI search?**
We can review a set of questions your potential customers are likely to ask and show you which businesses appear in the responses.

# Technical SEO Services & Website Audits

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/seo/technical-seo

> Find and fix technical website issues affecting search visibility, including indexing errors, slow pages, redirects, duplicate content, and site structure.

## Make sure your website can be found and indexed

Even strong website content can struggle in search results when pages aren't being indexed, the site is difficult to navigate, or technical issues interfere with how search engines access it. We identify those problems and help get them resolved.

### What is technical SEO?

Technical SEO deals with how your website is built and how search engines access its content. It includes indexing, page performance, redirects, mobile usability, internal linking, duplicate content, and structured data.
These issues aren't always obvious when you're browsing the site yourself. A page might look perfectly normal but be blocked from indexing. An outdated redirect might send visitors to the wrong place. Two similar pages might be competing for the same search terms.
We review how the site actually functions, not just the score an automated audit tool assigns it.
- Indexing
- Page performance
- Redirects and broken links
- Mobile usability
- Internal linking
- Duplicate content
- Structured data

### Technical issues that can affect search performance

#### Pages missing from Google's index

Important pages may be blocked, marked as duplicates, or difficult for Google to discover. We investigate why they aren't appearing and what needs to change.

#### Slow page performance

Large images, unnecessary scripts, and certain plugins can make a website slow, especially on mobile devices. We look for improvements that make sense for the site.

#### Duplicate content and conflicting URLs

Old pages, inconsistent canonical tags, or multiple URLs targeting the same subject can create confusion about which page should appear in search.

#### Broken links and redirects

Links to deleted pages and long redirect chains make navigation harder for visitors and can create unnecessary crawling issues.

#### Structured data problems

We review relevant structured data to make sure it accurately reflects the business and page content. Incorrect or unsupported markup can cause problems rather than help.

#### Content that is difficult to access

Some website features rely heavily on scripts or interactions. We check whether important content is available to search engines and other relevant crawlers.

### How we work

- 1 Audit the website We crawl the site and review available Google Search Console data for indexing, performance, and other technical issues.
- 2 Investigate the findings We look at the site's setup, templates, plugins, links, and redirects to understand what's causing the problems.
- 3 Prioritize the work We separate issues that need attention from lower impact recommendations, so you know what should be fixed first.
- 4 Make or coordinate fixes Depending on how your website is managed, we can implement approved changes or work with your developer on the required updates.
- 5 Keep an eye on performance We continue checking for new issues and review the impact of completed work.

### Find out what's affecting your website's search performance

We'll review the technical health of your site and help you prioritize the issues worth addressing.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**How is technical SEO different from other SEO services?**
Content SEO focuses on what your pages say and which searches they're relevant to. Technical SEO focuses on whether those pages can be found, indexed, and understood properly. Both are important.

**My SEO audit tool gives my website a high score. Do I still need an audit?**
Possibly. Automated scores don't always reflect the importance of an issue. A problem preventing a major service page from being indexed may matter far more than dozens of minor warnings. We explain more in Why an SEO Score Is Not the Same Thing as an SEO Strategy .

**Do you need access to my website?**
We can perform an initial public facing review without website access. Google Search Console access helps us investigate indexing and search performance in more detail. Making changes generally requires website access or coordination with your developer.

**Does website speed affect SEO?**
Page performance is one of several factors that can affect search. It also matters to visitors. A faster, easier to use site can improve the experience for people who arrive through any marketing channel.

**Does technical SEO help with AI search?**
It can. If important content is inaccessible to a crawler, that limits the information it can retrieve. Technical improvements help make your site easier for search systems to access, though they don't guarantee inclusion in AI generated answers.

# Website Migration SEO Services

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/seo/website-migration

> Redesigning your website, changing domains, or moving platforms? Protect existing search visibility with URL mapping, redirects, launch checks, and post launch monitoring.

## Protect your search traffic when you launch a new website

A new website should be an improvement, not a reason to lose the search visibility you've already built. We help businesses plan redesigns, domain changes, and platform moves with SEO in mind from the beginning.

### What is a website migration?

A website migration is a significant change to your site that can affect how search engines find and index its pages. It might involve changing domains, moving to a different platform, reorganizing URLs, or combining multiple websites.
These projects involve more than transferring content. Existing pages may already rank for valuable searches or have links from other websites. When those pages are removed or renamed without a proper plan, search engines and visitors can end up at missing or unrelated URLs.
We help map out those changes before launch and monitor the site afterward, so problems can be identified and addressed quickly.
- Changing domains
- Moving to a new platform
- Reorganizing URLs
- Combining multiple websites

### Common reasons for a migration

#### Website redesigns

Especially when the redesign changes URLs, navigation, or page structure.

#### Platform changes

Moving between WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, or another website platform.

#### Domain changes

Updating your website address as part of a rebrand or business change.

#### Website consolidations

Combining separate brands, locations, or websites into one.

#### Major URL or protocol changes

Reorganizing large sections of a website or correcting HTTP/HTTPS and www configurations.

### How we work

- 1 Review the existing website We gather the current URLs and use available analytics, Search Console data, and backlink information to identify important pages.
- 2 Plan the new URL structure We match old pages to relevant destinations on the new site and document the redirects needed for launch.
- 3 Check the new site before launch We review staging pages for missing content, broken links, metadata issues, indexing restrictions, and other potential problems.
- 4 Support the launch We check redirects, submit the appropriate sitemap, and handle applicable Search Console steps for a domain move.
- 5 Monitor the transition We watch indexing, traffic, rankings, and errors after launch, investigate unexpected changes, and make adjustments where needed.
- 6 Update important external links We identify business profiles, directory listings, and other important references that should point to the new site.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### Run Your Visibility Score

See how your business shows up in local search. We’ll email your results, no obligation.

#### Send Us a Message

We respond by the next business day. Your information is never shared.

### Redesigning or moving your website?

Bring us into the planning process early. We'll help identify the pages and search visibility that need to be protected during the move.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**Will my website lose rankings after a redesign?**
Not necessarily. Some movement is possible after a major change, but a well planned migration can reduce avoidable problems. The amount of disruption depends on what changes and how the transition is handled.

**How long should redirects stay in place?**
Google generally recommends keeping redirects for at least a year after a site move. Where practical, keeping redirects longer can continue to help people using old links, especially if you still own the previous domain.

**When should we involve an SEO team?**
Ideally, before the new website's page structure and URLs are finalized. It's easier to plan around existing search performance than to investigate lost traffic after launch.

**Can you work with our website developer?**
Yes. We can prepare the URL mapping, redirect requirements, and SEO launch checklist for your developer, or coordinate more of the implementation when we're involved in the website project.

**What if we've already launched and traffic has dropped?**
We can review what changed, compare old and new URLs, check indexing and redirects, and look for the likely causes. Some problems can be corrected, although recovery time and results will vary.

# Google Ads Management Services

## Get Found By Customers Ready to Buy

### Managed by Experts Since 2005

Most business owners just don't have the time to correctly manage their Google Ads, which leads to unproductive, expensive campaigns — or turning off the ads altogether. We have been managing Google Ad campaigns since 2005, and they don't look anything like they did back then.

# Branding & Logo Design Services

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/branding

> YB Marketing designs complete branding and graphics packages, including logos, brand identity, and visual systems, for businesses across the country. Ready for a brand that stands out? Call 509-901-9735.

## Elevate Your Brand Identity

Your brand is more than a logo — it's a complete visual language. We craft strategy, story, design systems, and deliverables that bring consistency, efficiency, and scalability to everything you put in front of customers.

### How to Elevate Your Brand Identity

We believe great design starts with understanding your brand and your unique story. Our team takes the time to discuss with you — and even your clients — the journey, values, and differentiators that set your business apart.
With our expertise in brand strategy, user experience, and scalable design, we help businesses establish a seamless, professional presence across every platform. Consistency builds trust. Trust builds brands.
Our process moves from discovery through design and delivery — refining strategy, story, and visual language until every touchpoint feels cohesive.
We combine brand visioning, research, journey mapping, and design system development so your spoken, written, and visual identity work together from day one.
We believe that great design starts with understanding your story. Our team takes the time to discuss with you — and even your clients — the unique journey, values, and differentiators that set your business apart.
By uncovering what makes your brand truly special, we ensure your design system authentically reflects your company's identity and resonates with your audience.
A brand is more than just a logo, but the logo is the most identifiable component of a brand and its identity. It is very much like a fingerprint and needs to be as uniquely differentiating.
When designed well, a logo tells your brand's story — conveying a message that helps establish an emotional connection with your target audience. It should grow out of your strategy, big idea, and story to complete your uniquely differentiating spoken, written, and visual language.
Our design systems include your brand story, typography, color, iconography, UI components, photography direction, and layout standards — all tailored to your unique business needs.
By centralizing your visual and digital assets, we empower your team to create cohesive marketing materials, websites, and applications without guesswork or inconsistencies.
Your logo is the most visible manifestation of your company within a target audience — which is why consistent, cohesive, and congruent use is so important.
Guidelines ensure that with each and every use of the logo, you are building upon your brand. Like a fingerprint, it should never be altered in ways that change your brand's identity or the perception you want your audience to hold.
Graphic standards provide a sound, flexible structure for using logos, color, typography, and other brand language. Consistent brand application is essential — logos and brand elements must appear the same in every instance.
They must use proper color selections, proportions, contexts, tone, style, and voice. The standards are often more important than the logo itself — because brands that aren't consistent can seem messy, untrustworthy, and unlikeable.
Print creates visual consistency, conveying a brand's personality and building trust and credibility outside the digital platform. Business cards, brochures, promos, and more can use unique finishes, textures, die cuts, and color that jumps off the page.
Print engages senses that digital content cannot simulate — making it the perfect complement to digital for a holistic branding and marketing campaign.
Great packaging creates an immediate point-of-purchase emotional connection in today's fast-paced, fiercely competitive marketplace. Color, shape, and materials play a critical role in brand recognition and differentiation.
Most products are known by the design of their packaging — like a hen's egg, a work of art, a masterpiece of design and simply brilliant packaging.
Signs represent a brand's most visible form of communication. Outdoor and indoor signage along with window graphics can impact how a brick-and-mortar location is perceived in the non-digital world.
Customers make assumptions about a business according to the quality and attractiveness of their signs — and that assumption carries over to how they perceive the quality of your products or services. All signs point to success.
Environmental Graphic Design (EGD) revolves around the strategic placement and design of visual elements to communicate information, evoke emotions, and guide behavior within interior and exterior spaces.
EGD creates visually compelling, functional experiences using color, imagery, typography, sound, and integrated three-dimensional elements — a fascinating intersection of graphic design, architecture, lighting, and landscape.
Good web design is essential to user interface and user experience — leading to longer site visits and improved engagement. Your website has become the primary platform for initial brand contact, so it must communicate your image consistently and cohesively.
We extend your brand's family look and feel online so you continue to be seen as viable, credible, and trusted. This is where code meets creative thinking.
Ready to transform your brand's visual identity? Let's start building a design system that grows with you.

### Brands Built on Strategy, Story & Design

Consistency builds trust — and trust builds brands. YB helps you develop a uniquely differentiating spoken, written, and visual language that unifies your business across print, digital, signage, and every customer touchpoint.

#### Discovery & Brand Visioning

### Frequently Asked Questions

**What is branding?**
Branding is the way your business presents itself to customers, including your logo, colors, messaging, tone, visuals, and overall identity.

**Why is branding important for my business?**
Strong branding helps people recognize, remember, and trust your business. It also makes your marketing more consistent across your website, ads, social media, and printed materials.

**What branding services do you offer?**
We can help with logo design, brand messaging, color palettes, typography, visual direction, brand guidelines, print materials, and digital brand assets.

**Do I need a new logo or a full brand refresh?**
It depends on your current brand. Some businesses only need small updates, while others benefit from a full refresh if their logo, messaging, or visuals feel outdated or inconsistent.

**What is included in a brand identity?**
A brand identity often includes your logo, colors, fonts, imagery style, messaging, tone of voice, and rules for how your brand should appear across different platforms.

**Can you help make our brand more consistent?**
Yes. We can review your current materials and create a more consistent look and message across your website, social media, ads, business cards, brochures, signage, and other marketing.

**How does branding help with marketing?**
Branding gives your marketing a clear foundation. When your visuals and messaging are consistent, your campaigns look more professional and are easier for customers to recognize.

**When should a business consider rebranding?**
A rebrand may make sense if your business has changed, your audience has shifted, your visuals feel outdated, your messaging is unclear, or your current brand no longer reflects the quality of your work.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**What is a press release?**

**Can you distribute the press release?**

**How long should a press release be?**

**Are press releases only for large companies?**
No. Small and local businesses can use press releases to announce meaningful updates, build credibility, and increase visibility in their market.

**Do you build chatbots or voice agents?**
Yes. We can help design and deploy assistants that answer common questions and capture leads.

**Will AI replace our marketing team?**
No. AI works best as a multiplier. It helps with faster drafts, better follow up, and clearer reporting alongside human strategy.

**How do you keep AI accurate and on brand?**
We set prompts, review workflows, and approve messaging so outputs stay aligned with your brand and offers.

**How quickly can we start using AI?**
Many teams see useful workflows within weeks once goals and tools are chosen.

**Is AI support ongoing?**
Yes. We can train your team, refine automations, and adjust as tools and needs change.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**Why did you go into Internet Marketing?**
In 2003, the Internet was still young. We were moving past dial-up, Google was just getting started, and laptops didn't really exist. But the future was obvious — the Internet was the place to be. I wanted to start my own company to help clients grow by using this new technology.

**What is your management philosophy?**
We do all we can to help the customer. We educate our customers as to what we think are the best steps and methods to help them achieve their goals. We do not chase the latest technologies — we may be slower to latch onto the next trend so we understand how something works best.

**What motivates you?**
I enjoy talking to customers who put their faith in us to help them grow. The Internet can be a scary place for some business owners — but our systems and tools are time-tested. We follow up, we communicate, and we admit when we need to fix something.

**What Internet Marketing technique is best for my business?**
That depends on your industry, demographic, ideal customer, and brand voice. It can be a mix of several platforms. Each platform delivers to a specific group — reach out so we can determine which will deliver you the best results.

**Are you more expensive than other agencies?**
We are different in that we do not try to be the cheapest agency. We trust our systems and services and can show using real data that they work. It is not about what you are paying — it is about what we can make for you. Low pricing is forgotten once you get the deal; low performance is felt for a long time.

# Custom Home Builder Website & SEO Case Study

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/about/case-studies/custom-home-builder-website-seo

> How YB Marketing rebuilt the website and SEO for a Northern California custom home builder, growing traffic 75% and search visibility 108% in one year.

## A Custom Home Builder Had Beautiful Work. Not Enough of the Right People Were Seeing It.

Our client is an experienced Northern California custom home builder that specializes in renovating a style of home first designed in the 1950s and 60s.
Their photos of past projects were stunning, but the website was dated, hard to update, and not built to win new clients from Google. They asked us to help more people see their work and request quotes.
A new website, better service content, and a steady blog grew traffic 75% and search visibility 108% in one year, and brought in the kind of leads they actually wanted.

### Start With the Competition

Our first step was a competitive analysis of other home renovation businesses in their area. We looked at website quality, search competition, advertising and social media.
That review led to a plan that was affordable and focused. This builder didn't need hundreds of leads. They needed a few good ones each month from homeowners looking for their specific style of work who could afford it.

### A Website That Matches the Work

Plenty of people search every day for what this company does, but weak content and poor SEO were pushing the site down the rankings. Over a few months we built a new website that shows off the craftsmanship and innovation behind every renovation and custom build.
Alongside the photography, we rewrote the service pages so they read well for homeowners and for search engines. We started a blog about the home styles they specialize in and put more emphasis on the areas they serve.

### The Results

The new site set a new standard for home builders in the area, with great photos and stories, video testimonials, and tours with happy clients.
Search engines responded with more relevant, higher quality traffic. Local rankings grew beyond the builder's own town into other areas where their style of home is common.

### What's Next

We keep adding blog posts and finding new keywords that bring in relevant leads. Social media is next. It usually has a longer buying cycle, but it plants seeds with future clients.
Is your website doing justice to your work? YB Marketing builds sites and SEO programs for builders and contractors.

# EMS Contract Manufacturer Google Ads & SEO Case Study

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/about/case-studies/ems-contract-manufacturer-google-ads-seo

> How YB Marketing grew a Silicon Valley EMS contract manufacturer from a small ad budget to nationwide reach, with traffic up 75% and visibility up 108% in one year.

## A Small Electronics Manufacturer Had a Tiny Budget and Big Plans. We Started Small and Grew With Them.

Our client was a small Silicon Valley electronics manufacturing company with funding and a talented team of engineers. They wanted to move into their own facility and build products themselves instead of designing solutions and outsourcing production.
We met them early, when the marketing budget was as small as the company, and recommended starting small.
Targeted Google Ads paid for the first round of growth. Later, a rebuilt website and SEO helped them reach hardware developers across the country as their ad budget grew tenfold.

### Make the Website Work First

There was no budget for a rebuild at the start, so we cleaned up the existing site to make it easier to use. If we were going to send people there, they needed to understand what this company could do.

### Let Ads Pay for Growth

Once the site was ready, we launched tightly targeted Google Ads for specialized services and for buyers who needed quick turns and hands-on support. In short, we bootstrapped their marketing by using new business to fund more business.

### Rebuild as the Company Grew

As the business moved into its own office and manufacturing space, we rebuilt the website, added a blog, and built up their SEO. The company kept growing, taking over more of their building with new private funding made possible by their unique services and steady growth.

### The Results

With a tight budget early on, we spent our time only on the work that would get them moving. Over time the ad budget grew 10×, and we expanded SEO and ads to other parts of the country to reach hardware developers in other states.
Today they handle much larger production runs and are still known as experts in new materials development and fast, manufacturable engineering prototypes.
Working with a small budget and big goals? YB Marketing can build a plan that grows with you.

# Environmental Engineering Content Marketing Case Study: +93% Visibility

## An Environmental Engineering Firm Knew Its Content Mattered. It Just Never Got Written.

Our client, a California environmental engineering firm, had planned to start a content marketing program in house but never got it off the ground.
Their analytical and pollution remediation services are needed around the world, but their website had too little content and not enough focus.
A redesigned website and a steady flow of expert content grew traffic 57% and search visibility 93% in one year.

In those early conversations they also saw that we could help create quality content that works for search engines, social media and even printed marketing materials.

Traffic grew 57% and search visibility 93% in one year, and the results opened management's eyes to promoting new services with new content.
Know your expertise should be online but never find time to write it? YB Marketing plans and writes content that gets found.

# Equipment Manufacturer Website Redesign & SEO Case Study

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/about/case-studies/equipment-manufacturer-website-redesign

> How YB Marketing redesigned the website and SEO for a California automated assembly equipment manufacturer, growing traffic 75% and visibility 108% in one year.

## An Equipment Manufacturer With 50 Years of Engineering Had a Website That Didn't Show It.

Our client is a California company that designs, engineers and builds automated product assembly equipment. They've been in business since the 1970s and helped develop processes still used across the industry today.
Their market is mature and highly competitive. What sets them apart is engineering skill and the repeatability and reliability of their equipment, but their old website didn't show it.
A mobile friendly redesign and new application focused content replaced off-topic traffic with qualified visitors and leads, growing traffic 75% and search visibility 108% in one year.

### The Challenge

We had worked with them on several projects over the years before they decided to get serious about digital marketing. Their website was old and dusty, and much of its traffic had nothing to do with their core business.

### The Approach

We redesigned the website so it worked on mobile and was much easier to read. The company supplied most of the core content, and we added our SEO knowledge so Google could understand, index and show it to the right buyers.
We also started adding content on applications, industries and the problems their equipment solves. The goal was to show prospects that this company's knowledge and approach to engineering is unique. We run occasional targeted Google Ads for trade shows and specific services as needed.

### The Results

The new site gave search engines and visitors clearer, more complete content. Traffic, time on site and leads all showed the plan worked, and it's still working today.
Does your website undersell your engineering? YB Marketing builds sites and content for manufacturers that bring in qualified leads.

# Fortune 500 Multilingual Accessibility Remediation

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/about/case-studies/fortune-500-multilingual-accessibility

> How YB Marketing turned a Fortune 500 accessibility audit into shipped fixes across three domains and six languages — React, brand tokens, and translation pipeline included.

## A Fortune 500 Accessibility Audit Identified the Issues. Implementing Them Across Six Languages Was the Real Work.

A Fortune 500 enterprise had commissioned a third-party accessibility audit across their global web presence. Three domains, each published in six languages. The audit returned a thorough inventory of issues. It did not return a way to fix them without affecting brand consistency, translation coverage, or the working experience of the live sites.
That gap was where the project lived. The audit said what was wrong. Remediation was the body of work that had to take those findings and ship them into production cleanly, across three domains and six locales, with each fix verified in every language before it went live.
Over a few months we took the audit from report to implementation. Three domains, six languages, conformant at the end of it, with the brand intact.

### The Situation

The client owned three domains: a primary corporate site and two supporting properties serving distinct business functions. Each was published in six languages. The audit had been performed against all three.
The findings spanned the surface area you would expect at this scale: contrast failures inside brand-owned colour tokens, interactive components without keyboard or screen reader support, forms with missing programmatic labels and silent error states, carousels that played without controls, video without captions, and a long list of third-party embeds (PDFs, maps, and other inserted content) that arrived on the page without any accessibility scaffolding around them.
None of the individual issues were exotic. What made the remediation work substantial was the combination they sat inside. A Fortune 500 web presence with brand tokens that could not be casually edited. Three connected domains. Six language versions of every fix. And a meaningful portion of the interactive surface rendered through React components.

### Why Remediation Was the Hard Part

An audit is a static document. Remediation is the part that has to ship. On a multilingual estate with this kind of reach, that distinction matters.

#### Brand-owned colour and contrast tokens

Several contrast failures sat inside colour tokens that were part of the client's global brand system. We could not unilaterally darken a brand colour. Each contrast adjustment had to be resolved at the usage layer (changing the background a token sat on, increasing font weight, switching to a different approved token, adjusting state colours for links, buttons, and focus) or escalated to the brand owners for an approved tonal variant.
This part of the work was as much coordination as code. Each proposed change went through brand review before reaching the staging environment.

#### React-rendered interactive components

The most demanding piece of the remediation was the interactive layer rendered through React. These components had been built for visual behaviour first and accessibility second. Roles were missing or wrong, state changes were not announced, focus was lost on re-render, and keyboard interaction worked partially or not at all depending on which sub-component was active.
Each component needed a real rebuild of its accessibility model. Roles, names, and states declared correctly. Focus surviving re-renders and routing back to a sensible place when modals, drawers, and overlays closed. State changes that mattered to a screen reader user (selections, expansions, errors, loading) announced through live regions without flooding them. None of this could be applied uniformly across components because each one had its own state model.

#### Dropdowns, forms, and error states

Forms across all three domains relied on a mix of native and custom dropdown controls. Native selects worked. The custom dropdowns, the styled ones the design system preferred, were the ones flagged by the audit. They needed correct roles, keyboard operation, programmatic state, and accessible names that flowed through the translation pipeline.
The error-state work was equally material. Failing fields needed programmatic association between the error message and the input, the message itself had to be announced when it appeared, and required-field status had to be exposed correctly rather than left as a visual asterisk. Each fix was translated and verified across all six locales.

#### Carousels and slideshows

The carousels on the site autoplayed, did not expose a pause control to assistive technology, did not handle keyboard navigation cleanly, and lost focus when slides changed. Each of these is an individual fix in isolation. Together, they meant the carousel components had to be re-architected, not just patched. Pause and play controls exposed properly. Slide changes announced where it mattered. Focus managed when users interacted with controls. Reduced-motion preferences respected.

#### Embedded content: video, PDFs, and maps

A meaningful portion of the page content was not owned by the client's sites at all. Videos were embedded from external players. PDFs were either linked or embedded inside iframes. Maps were embedded from a third-party provider. The source documents could not be edited as part of the engagement.
What could be fixed was the embedding itself. Videos were configured to load with captions available and player controls exposed to assistive technology. PDF links and embeds were rewritten so the purpose, file type, and behaviour were clear to a screen reader user before the link was activated, with proper iframe titles where PDFs were displayed inline. Map embeds received accessible names, were taken out of the keyboard tab order where they trapped focus, and were paired with text-based alternatives (address, directions, contact) so the underlying information was reachable without the map widget itself being usable.

#### Images across six languages

Alt text gaps were spread across the asset library, and they were not symmetrical between language versions. Some images had alt text in English and nothing in the other five locales. Others were decorative on some pages and meaningful on others. Closing this required a per-locale pass, not a single global change.

#### Six language versions of every fix

Every accessible name, helper text string, error message, and announcement we introduced during the project had to exist in all six languages. Hardcoded English strings were not an option. Each new label and message was routed through the translation pipeline, registered in the site's translation memory, and verified in every locale before the fix was considered shipped.

#### Working across development, staging, and production

The team had a development environment, a staging environment, and production. Each change moved through that pipeline before reaching live users, which removed the risk of shipping a broken fix into a Fortune 500 web presence directly. What it did not remove was the locale multiplication. A fix that passed verification in English on staging still had to be checked in German, where compound words ran longer and could wrap where they did not in English, and in each of the other four locales. Promotion to production was paced so that no business unit was caught out by a layout shift in their language.

### The Gap Between the Audit and the Work

The audit document listed issues. It did not say, for each issue, which of the three domains it appeared on, which of the six languages it affected, which component generated it, or what the downstream consequences of fixing it would be. Building that mapping was the first piece of real work.
Some audit findings, written generically, turned out to be a single shared component used in dozens of places. Fixing the component fixed every instance. Other findings, written as a single issue, were actually six instances (one per language) because the translated DOM diverged from the source in ways the audit had not captured. The audit's count of issues and the count of actual fixes did not match in either direction.
We rebuilt the issue list as a remediation plan organised by template, component, embed type, and locale. Fixes that could be made at the code layer were separated from those that required translation work, brand approval, or third-party embed configuration. That plan was what the rest of the engagement worked from.

### What We Did

The work moved in tracks that ran in parallel where they could and serialised where they could not. Each track was scoped, executed, verified across all six locales on staging, and promoted to production before the next batch began.

#### Colour and contrast adjustments

Contrast failures were resolved through usage-layer changes wherever possible, and through brand-approved tonal variants where a token itself had to change. Focus, hover, disabled, and error states across links, buttons, and form fields were brought up to conformance, with the brand team signing off on each change before it shipped.

#### React component rebuilds

The interactive components rendered through React were the most concentrated body of work. Each component received a proper accessibility model: roles, accessible names, states, keyboard operation, focus management on mount and unmount, and announcements for the state changes that mattered to a screen reader user. Components were tested both in isolation and inside the pages that used them.

#### Forms and dropdowns

Forms across all three domains were rebuilt to associate labels programmatically with their inputs, expose required-field status correctly, announce errors when they appeared, and provide error text that screen readers could associate with the failing field. Custom dropdowns received correct roles, keyboard handling, and accessible names. Native dropdowns were left in place where they already worked.

#### Carousels and slideshows

Carousel components were re-architected to expose pause and play controls, support keyboard navigation, manage focus when slides changed, and respect reduced-motion preferences. Autoplay behaviour was reviewed against the requirement that users have meaningful control over moving content.

#### Video accessibility

Embedded video was configured to load with captions available and player controls exposed to assistive technology. Where videos were used to convey information not available elsewhere on the page, the embedding was paired with a textual fallback.

#### PDF, map, and other embed remediation

PDFs were not edited at the source. What changed was the way they were referenced from the sites: link text describing the document and its file type, iframe titles where PDFs were embedded inline, and clear indication of behaviour before the link was activated. Map embeds received accessible names, were prevented from trapping keyboard focus, and were paired with text-based alternatives so the underlying information was reachable without the map widget.

#### Image and alt text coverage

The asset library was reviewed per locale. Missing alt text was added in each language, decorative images were marked correctly, and image variants that differed between language versions received translated alt text rather than a default fallback.

#### Translation pipeline updates

Every new accessible name, helper text, and announcement introduced during remediation was translated into all six languages and registered in the site's translation memory. Nothing was left as a hardcoded English string. The pipeline was extended so future content and feature work would inherit the same coverage.

#### Cross-locale verification

Every change went through a verification pass on staging in all six languages before being promoted to production. Automated tooling caught the structural failures (contrast, missing attributes, broken hierarchies). Manual testing covered the parts that required judgement: keyboard flow through React components, announcements firing at the right moment, error handling in real forms, and embed behaviour for video, PDFs, and maps.

### The Outcome

All three domains reached conformance across all six languages within the engagement window. The brand system remained intact. The translation pipeline was extended cleanly to cover the new accessibility surface. No business unit experienced a regression in their language during the rollout.
The internal documentation produced during the project (the remediation plan, the per-locale verification notes, the component-level guidance) was handed back to the client's web and brand teams so future content and feature work would stay inside the conformance envelope rather than drifting back out of it.

### What This Means for Multilingual Enterprise Sites

If you run a multilingual web estate at enterprise scale, the patterns that made this engagement substantial are likely already present in your environment.

#### The audit is the start of the work

A WCAG audit identifies issues. It does not tell you which component generates them, which language variants are affected, which fixes require brand approval, or which fixes will ripple through translation. Building that map is its own piece of work and is usually where remediation projects stall.

#### Multilingual makes every fix wider

A single accessibility fix on a monolingual site is one change. The same fix on a six-language site can be six changes, each with its own translation, layout, and verification requirements. Scoping accessibility work without accounting for locale multiplication is how timelines slip.

#### Custom React components carry most of the work

Custom interactive components rendered through React rarely behave correctly for assistive technology without a deliberate rebuild. Surface patches do not solve focus loss on re-render, missing state announcements, or broken keyboard models. The component has to be reworked, which is a different cost profile to fixing static markup.

#### Brand sign-off has to be in scope from the start

Contrast failures often live inside brand-owned colour tokens. Remediation that does not include the brand team in the loop either ships changes the brand will later roll back, or stalls indefinitely waiting for approval that was never requested correctly.

#### You can fix the embedding when you cannot fix the source

Videos, PDFs, and maps that arrive on the page from third-party sources often cannot be edited at the source. What can be fixed is the way they are embedded: link text, iframe titles, focus behaviour, and text-based alternatives that put the underlying information within reach of someone who cannot use the widget itself.

#### Conformance drifts without ongoing ownership

A site reaches conformance and then drifts out of it the next time a new feature ships, a new template is added, or a new piece of content is published without translation coverage on its accessible names. The handover documentation is what determines whether the work holds.
Sitting on an accessibility audit you have not yet implemented? YB Marketing remediates multilingual enterprise sites at scale, takes audit findings from inventory to shipped conformance, and hands back the documentation your team needs to stay there.

# Local Electrical Contractor SEO Case Study, +112% Organic Traffic

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/about/case-studies/local-electrical-contractor-seo-growth

> How YB Marketing grew organic search traffic 112% year over year, search impressions 366% at peak, and page-one keyword rankings 204% for a Greater Bay Area electrical contractor.

## A Local Electrical Contractor Had the Crews and the Reputation. Organic Search Wasn't Sending the Calls.

### 2024 vs. 2025 snapshot

A growing electrical contracting business in the Greater Bay Area — serving both residential and commercial customers — had a functional website but almost no organic search visibility outside of its own brand name. New customer acquisition relied almost entirely on paid advertising and subcontractor referrals.
As costs rose and lead volume swung month to month, the client needed a repeatable channel that could generate qualified calls for high-value work: panel upgrades, rewiring, EV charger installation, and emergency electrical repair.
Over roughly two years, we built a full-funnel local SEO program — service and location pages, local authority signals, and monthly rank tracking. Annual organic search traffic rose 112% year over year, search impressions grew 366% at peak, and page-one keyword coverage grew 204%.

### The Challenge

The business had a solid reputation and busy crews, but organic search was effectively limited to branded queries. Paid ads and referrals drove most new work — both with rising costs and uneven volume.
The client needed a lower-cost, repeatable channel that could surface the business for urgent, high-intent searches — panel upgrades, commercial wiring, emergency repair — without relying on the ad budget alone.

### The Strategy

We implemented a full-funnel local SEO program built to convert search visibility directly into phone calls and quote requests:

#### Service + location page expansion

dedicated pages for panel upgrades, EV charger installation, commercial wiring, emergency repair, and every market served.

#### Local authority building

strengthening Google Business Profile signals and local citations to compete for map-pack and "near me" searches.

#### Ongoing rank monitoring

tracking keyword position and lead volume monthly to double down on what was converting.

### Organic Traffic Growth

Monthly organic search traffic rose 112% year over year, with a peak monthly gain of 167% above the February 2025 baseline by October 2025.

### Search Impressions

Google Search Console impressions grew 366% from the February 2025 baseline to the August 2025 peak. Six-month impression growth hit 212% by July before settling into a sustained baseline roughly 3× the starting point.

### Keyword Rankings

Page 1 keyword rankings grew 204% since tracking began, with the client also establishing a meaningful presence in emerging AI-powered search placements — a category that didn't exist for this business two years ago.

### Why It Matters

For a contractor whose business depends on a steady pipeline of new service calls, growing organic visibility is the difference between constantly buying traffic and owning a channel that compounds over time.
The impression and organic traffic growth map directly to more qualified discovery — the searches that turn into phone calls and quote requests.
Need local SEO that turns search visibility into service calls? YB Marketing builds programs for contractors — service pages, map-pack authority, and rank tracking included.

# 130-Site WordPress Malware Remediation

URL: https://yakimabranding.com/about/case-studies/wordpress-portfolio-malware-remediation

> How YB Marketing cleaned a 130-site WordPress portfolio infected with ad-click-only malware, got Google Ads reinstated, and achieved zero reinfections in three months.

## A 130-Site WordPress Portfolio Looked Clean. Google Ads Knew Something Was Wrong.

An agency owner who had just taken over a 130-site WordPress portfolio found their Google Ads accounts getting suspended repeatedly, with no obvious cause. Every site looked clean. Every scanner returned clear results. The infection had been running undetected across all 130 properties, silently redirecting paid ad traffic to rogue domains while evading every automated check.
For the new owner, this was not just a security problem. It was a client-retention problem, a paid-media problem, and a trust problem. Each suspension made them look responsible for a situation they had inherited and could not yet explain. We were brought in to find the cause, clean the portfolio, and make sure it stayed clean.
In 15 days, the full portfolio was cleaned, hardened, and documented for Google Ads review. Three months later, all 130 sites remain stable, with no reinfections and no recurring ad suspensions.

### The Situation

A client brought us in after taking over a 130-site WordPress portfolio from a previous agency. Every site in the portfolio was running Google Ads. Within weeks of the handover, ad accounts began getting flagged and suspended for policy violations, one after another. For an agency owner trying to establish trust with 130 clients from day one, the timing could not have been worse. The sites loaded perfectly. Traffic patterns looked normal. There were no error messages, no visitor complaints, no server alerts. Yet every single property was compromised. The infection had been running completely undetected.

### Why Nobody Caught It

Most malware announces itself. This one was built to do the opposite.

#### The hidden plugin

The infection came in the form of a PHP plugin with a generic, unremarkable name. It installed itself like any other plugin but used a WordPress filter to remove itself from the admin plugins screen. There was nothing to find in the dashboard. The only way to spot it was through FTP or direct server access. Standard plugin audits, the kind most agencies run, came back clean.
The delivery server only served actual JavaScript to browsers that arrived with active Google Ads session signals. Security scanners got a blank file. Automated crawlers got a blank file. Anyone opening the script URL in a browser tab got a blank file. Every scan said clean because, to every scan, it was. The only people who saw what the malware was actually doing were the ones clicking through from paid ads.

#### Hidden admin access

Built into the plugin was a hardcoded backdoor. Passing a specific GET parameter in a URL would immediately log the attacker in as the site's first administrator, with no password, no two-factor prompt, nothing. One request. Full access. This meant the attacker could return to any site at any time, regardless of how many times passwords had been reset.

#### Unauthorised file writes

The plugin registered a REST API endpoint open to anyone on the internet. No authentication was required. Through this endpoint, an attacker could push arbitrary PHP code directly into theme files on the site. The plugin also actively cleared all major caching plugins after each write, so injected code would be live and serving to real visitors within seconds.

#### Ad-click-only redirects

On every page load, the plugin made a server-side call to an external server, retrieved a base64-encoded URL, decoded it, and injected a script tag at the very top of the page before any other content was sent to the visitor.
Every visitor loaded this script on every page. The redirect logic inside it only fired for visitors who had just clicked a Google Ad. Direct visitors, organic traffic, anyone browsing normally saw nothing wrong.
The destination URL was never stored on the site. It was pulled fresh from the attacker's server on each page load. The delivery domain rotated every day or two. So the cycle ran like this: Google flags a URL and suspends the account, the client moves through reinstatement, the account goes back live, the ads run again, Google flags the new domain, the account is suspended again. The infection kept running through every reinstatement because nobody knew to look for it.
The data-cfasync='false' attribute on the script tag was not accidental. It instructs Cloudflare's Rocket Loader to leave the script alone, which meant the malicious code ran before any Cloudflare processing could touch it.

#### Built-in reinfection mechanism

We learned early on that simply deleting the plugin was not enough. The malware had already embedded a reinstaller into wp-cron.php that could recreate a fresh copy of itself under a different directory name. It had also embedded AES-256 encrypted PHP payloads inside files in the theme's /patterns/ directory, files that looked like ordinary template files to anyone browsing the folder. Those payloads would only execute if the attacker passed the right decryption key via URL parameters.
We cleaned one site and deliberately left it without the additional security layer to see what would happen. It was re-infected within 24 hours. That test shaped everything that followed.

### Where the Infection Came From

The evidence pointed to a compromised WordPress management tool used across the portfolio. Because the same tool was connected to all 130 sites, the exposure spread portfolio-wide. Several of the sites had Wordfence installed and active throughout. It did not detect the infection or prevent re-infection.
The delivery infrastructure revealed an operation with more reach than a single bad actor with a cheap server. The rotating domains hosting the malicious JavaScript files did not belong to the attacker. They were other compromised WordPress sites belonging to unrelated organisations that had no idea their servers were being used. One delivery domain we identified resolved to the same server as a well-known international non-profit. The attacker had added their domain as a virtual host, planted the file, used it for a couple of days, then moved on. By the time any investigation caught up to a particular domain, the file was already gone.

### What We Did

We worked through every site individually, completing the full sequence on each one before moving to the next. Partial work on a site was not an option given what the re-infection test had shown. The sequence on each site was file system remediation, database cleanup, credential rotation, and hardening. 130 sites over 15 days.

#### File system remediation

WordPress core files were reinstalled from verified checksums on every site. Non-core directories were inspected manually and cleared of unauthorised PHP files, including the encrypted payloads in the theme pattern directories and anything else that had no business being there. File editing through the WordPress admin was disabled at the configuration level to close that route for future writes.

#### Database remediation

The injected JavaScript strings were located and removed from the wp_posts and wp_options tables on each site's database. This required care to strip the malicious content without corrupting legitimate data. The conditional redirect hooks came out at the source.

#### Credential rotation and hardening

All active sessions were terminated, unauthorised admin accounts removed, and credentials rotated across every property. A consistent security configuration was then applied to each site to close the attack surfaces the malware had used: login protections, file permission changes, attack surface reduction across the WordPress configuration, and invalidation of all existing sessions. The configuration that had been missing from the re-infection test site was in place on all 130 by the end.

### The Outcome

Three months on, all 130 sites remain clean. No re-infections, no redirects, no rogue admin accounts.
We provided the technical remediation evidence the client needed to move through the Google Ads reinstatement process. Once the domains were verified clean and the documentation submitted, the accounts came back without the recurring suspensions that had defined the previous weeks.
There is now an ongoing engagement covering the full portfolio. High-profile sites get a weekly manual audit: file integrity checks, security log review, user account monitoring, and backup validation, with a written report after each session. The wider portfolio gets a monthly review cycle.
The reason the client wanted ongoing cover is straightforward. The infection ran without a single visible indicator for weeks. The only thing that flagged it was Google pulling the ad accounts. Once you have seen an attack run that quietly for that long, the question of whether your current setup would catch something similar becomes a lot harder to answer confidently.

### What This Means for Agency-Managed Portfolios

If you manage WordPress sites for clients who run paid advertising, the same conditions that allowed this infection are common across agency-managed portfolios.

#### There is no visible signal

The WordPress admin may look clean. The site may load normally. Scanners may report no issue. Paid traffic can still be compromised. Infections like this typically run for weeks before anything surfaces, and when they do, it is usually a Google Ads suspension that reveals it, not a security alert.

#### Your management tool can become a single point of failure

Centralised management is efficient, but if the tool is compromised, exposure can spread across every connected site simultaneously. The assumption that a trusted platform is safe to use is not the same as knowing it is.

#### Cleanup without hardening creates a loop

Removing malware is not the same as closing the entry point. In this case, a cleaned site without the added hardening layer was re-infected within 24 hours. The entry points have to be closed, or the cycle starts again.

#### Automated tools are not enough

This infection was designed to hide from scanners and the WordPress admin. Finding it required direct file system review, database inspection, and behavioural testing. Active security plugins on multiple sites detected nothing throughout the entire infection period.
Managing a WordPress portfolio with paid traffic behind it? YB Marketing helps agencies uncover hidden malware, recover compromised sites, and harden portfolios before silent infections turn into suspended ads, emergency calls, and client-retention problems.

---

**How long does it take to see results?**

Most businesses see real movement in three to six months, and competitive searches in the Bay Area can take closer to a year. A lot of our clients run both so the phone rings while SEO builds.

**Which channels make sense for a Bay Area business?**
For most Bay Area service businesses we start with Google Business Profile, local SEO, and tightly targeted Google Ads. Click prices are high here, so we spend time on negative keywords, call tracking, and landing pages before we scale spend.

**Do we need to be local to work with you?**
No. Our office is in Yakima, Washington, and we work with clients all over the country by phone, Zoom, and email. You'll have a direct line to the people doing the work, and we keep the same hours you do.

**Can you work with our in house marketing person?**
Yes. Some clients hand us everything. Others have someone in house and want help with SEO, ads, or the website. We'll fit around how you already work.

**Do you build websites too?**
Yes. We design and build websites on WordPress and Wix, and we can move your current site to a new one without losing your Google rankings.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**How long does it take to see results?**
Ads can bring in calls within the first couple of weeks, because you're paying for placement. SEO takes longer. Most businesses see real movement in three to six months, and competitive searches in Chicago can take closer to a year. A lot of our clients run both so the phone rings while SEO builds.

**Which channels make sense for a Chicago business?**
In a market this size, we almost always split the work by area. Local SEO and location pages for the neighborhoods and suburbs you serve, plus Google Ads with tight geographic targeting. B2B companies often add LinkedIn and content marketing.

**Do we need to be local to work with you?**
No. Our office is in Yakima, Washington, and we work with clients all over the country by phone, Zoom, and email. You'll have a direct line to the people doing the work, and we keep the same hours you do.

**How do you report on results?**
You get a monthly report in plain English: calls, form fills, rankings, ad spend, and what each lead cost. If you'd rather talk it through, we'll walk you through it on a call.

**Can you work with our in house marketing person?**
Yes. Some clients hand us everything. Others have someone in house and want help with SEO, ads, or the website. We'll fit around how you already work.

**Do you build websites too?**
Yes. We design and build websites on WordPress and Wix, and we can move your current site to a new one without losing your Google rankings.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**How long does it take to see results?**
Ads can bring in calls within the first couple of weeks, because you're paying for placement. SEO takes longer. Most businesses see real movement in three to six months, and competitive searches in Spokane can take closer to a year. A lot of our clients run both so the phone rings while SEO builds.

**Which channels make sense for a Spokane business?**
In a market Spokane's size, we usually pair local SEO with Google Ads targeted to the parts of town you serve. Call tracking shows which campaigns turn into booked jobs so the budget goes where it works.

**Can we meet in person?**
Yes. Our office is in Yakima, and we're happy to come to you for kickoff and planning meetings. Day to day, most of our work happens by phone, Zoom, and email.

**How do you report on results?**
You get a monthly report in plain English: calls, form fills, rankings, ad spend, and what each lead cost. If you'd rather talk it through, we'll walk you through it on a call.

**Can you work with our in house marketing person?**
Yes. Some clients hand us everything. Others have someone in house and want help with SEO, ads, or the website. We'll fit around how you already work.

**Do you build websites too?**
Yes. We design and build websites on WordPress and Wix, and we can move your current site to a new one without losing your Google rankings.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**How long does it take to see results?**
Ads can bring in calls within the first couple of weeks, because you're paying for placement. SEO takes longer. Most businesses see real movement in three to six months, and competitive searches in Boise can take closer to a year. A lot of our clients run both so the phone rings while SEO builds.

**Which channels make sense for a Boise business?**
Most Boise businesses start with Google Business Profile and local SEO, with Google Ads bringing in calls while rankings build. If you serve Meridian, Nampa, or Eagle, we add location pages so you show up there too.

**Do we need to be local to work with you?**
No. Our office is in Yakima, Washington, and we work with clients all over the country by phone, Zoom, and email. You'll have a direct line to the people doing the work, and we keep the same hours you do.

**How do you report on results?**
You get a monthly report in plain English: calls, form fills, rankings, ad spend, and what each lead cost. If you'd rather talk it through, we'll walk you through it on a call.

**Can you work with our in house marketing person?**
Yes. Some clients hand us everything. Others have someone in house and want help with SEO, ads, or the website. We'll fit around how you already work.

**Do you build websites too?**
Yes. We design and build websites on WordPress and Wix, and we can move your current site to a new one without losing your Google rankings.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**How long does it take to see results?**
Ads can bring in calls within the first couple of weeks, because you're paying for placement. SEO takes longer. Most businesses see real movement in three to six months, and competitive searches in Littleton can take closer to a year. A lot of our clients run both so the phone rings while SEO builds.

**Which channels make sense for a Littleton business?**
Most Littleton service businesses start with Google Business Profile and local SEO, plus pages for the nearby communities they serve. Google Ads targeted by zip code bring in calls while SEO builds.

**Do we need to be local to work with you?**
No. Our office is in Yakima, Washington, and we work with clients all over the country by phone, Zoom, and email. You'll have a direct line to the people doing the work, and we keep the same hours you do.

**How do you report on results?**
You get a monthly report in plain English: calls, form fills, rankings, ad spend, and what each lead cost. If you'd rather talk it through, we'll walk you through it on a call.

**Can you work with our in house marketing person?**
Yes. Some clients hand us everything. Others have someone in house and want help with SEO, ads, or the website. We'll fit around how you already work.

**Do you build websites too?**
Yes. We design and build websites on WordPress and Wix, and we can move your current site to a new one without losing your Google rankings.
